newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shekel gains against dlr in sleepy trade.
newsitem.headline: Israel shekel gains against dlr in sleepy trade.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose slightly against the dollar on Wednesday in lucklustre trading, dealers said.
"The market is very quiet today and trading is trendless. The shekel rose slightly but it was on a very low volume," said Guy Levi at Bank Leumi.
"The market is a little sleepy and volume is low. The shekel has no strength to rise or fall," said Olivier Hakoune at Union Bank.
"The market is still very nervous as it is looking for direction and spreads are still high at 70-100 points," Hakoune added.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5690 shekels against 3.5730 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8701 against 3.8794 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.1663 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.1704 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 2.0254 shekels compared with 2.0347 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5620 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
